subject: Geography
central_question: Why do natural and human-induced hazards become disasters in India, and how can vulnerability, loss and recovery be managed?
in_scope_units: Meaning of hazard, disaster and vulnerability.
Natural and human causes and classification of disasters.
Earthquakes, hazard zones, consequences and mitigation.
banned_topics: Detailed plate-boundary theory, which belongs to Distribution of Oceans and Continents.
Detailed monsoon seasons, which belong to Climate.
Detailed geomorphic-process classification, which belongs to Geomorphic Processes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every natural hazard is automatically a disaster.
known_pitfalls.correction: It becomes a disaster when impacts seriously disrupt life and exceed coping capacity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Disasters are caused only by natural forces.
known_pitfalls.correction: Human actions can directly cause disasters or intensify natural hazards.
They cannot be prevented; preparedness and mitigation reduce loss.

known_pitfalls.claim: Tsunamis are most dangerous in the deepest ocean.
known_pitfalls.correction: Their height and impact increase near shallow coasts.
The chapter includes meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and ecological drought.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise 2(i) to explain when a hazard becomes a disaster.
Use Exercise 2(iii) to state conditions for a tropical cyclone.
Use Exercise 3(i) to identify landslide-prone regions and mitigation.
Use Exercise 3(ii) to relate drought vulnerability to management.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Exercises 1(i–v), 2(i–v), 3(i–iii), and an eight-option Project/Activity.
